u0539.gist: Bhupender Yadav opened a national Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict at WII–SACON, Coimbatore, on July 10, 2026, and launched a national conflict portal.
facts: Inaugurated by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on July 10, 2026.
Location: WII–SACON (Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History), Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu.
He also launched the National Human–Wildlife Conflict Portal.
Released first edition of 'Current Status of Human–Wildlife Conflict in India: An Overview'.
u0539.trap: SACON is in Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu) and is a research institute of the Wildlife Institute of India.

mcq.q: Where was the national Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict inaugurated in July 2026?
mcq.why: It was set up at WII–SACON, Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, on July 10, 2026.

u0540.gist: On June 5, 2026, Bhupender Yadav and Delhi CM Rekha Gupta opened 18 Namo Oxygen Parks in Delhi under 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam'.
facts: Inaugurated June 5, 2026 (World Environment Day) by Bhupender Yadav and Delhi CM Rekha Gupta.
18 Namo Oxygen Parks opened across the national capital.
Part of the nationwide 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign.
Origin: in 2024 the DDA illegally cut over 1,100 mature trees in the Southern Ridge.
Southern Ridge: protected reserve forest called the 'lungs of the capital'.
u0540.trap: 18 = parks opened in 2026; 1,100 = trees illegally cut in 2024.

mcq.q: Under which campaign were 18 Namo Oxygen Parks inaugurated in Delhi on World Environment Day 2026?
mcq.why: The parks were opened under the nationwide 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign.

u0541.gist: Hardeep Singh Puri launched E85 fuel at an IndianOil outlet in New Delhi on June 5, 2026, moving India toward flex-fuel vehicles.
facts: Launched by Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri on June 5, 2026 (World Environment Day), New Delhi.
E85 = 80–85% ethanol + 14–19% petrol, made for flex-fuel vehicles.
Flex-fuel vehicles (FFVs) run on E20 to E100; engine detects ethanol content automatically.
E85 is priced nearly ₹20 per litre lower than petrol.
FFVs on E85 can cut lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions by around 61% vs petrol vehicles.
Blending rose from 1.53% (2014) to 20% (June 5, 2026), five years ahead of schedule.
u0541.hook: E85 launch day = World Environment Day (June 5).
u0541.trap: E85 is a high-ethanol fuel (80–85% ethanol); E20 is the normal 20% blend.

mcq.q: What is the ethanol content of the E85 fuel launched in India on June 5, 2026?
mcq.why: E85 has 80–85 per cent ethanol and 14–19 per cent petrol.

mcq.q: By around how much can flex-fuel vehicles running on E85 cut lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions compared with petrol vehicles?
mcq.why: FFVs on E85 can reduce lifecycle GHG emissions by around 61 per cent.

u0542.gist: In May 2026, the Andaman and Nicobar Administration set two underwater Guinness World Records at Swaraj Dweep to promote scuba and marine tourism.
facts: Two underwater Guinness World Records set in May 2026 at Swaraj Dweep.
Swaraj Dweep was earlier known as Havelock Island (South Andaman).
First record: 'Largest flag unfurled underwater' (Indian Tricolour).
Second record: 'Tallest human stack underwater'.
Record holder: Andaman and Nicobar Administration; aim: scuba, marine and responsible adventure tourism.
u0542.hook: Havelock Island → Swaraj Dweep: old name, new name.

mcq.q: At which island did the Andaman and Nicobar Administration set two underwater Guinness World Records in May 2026?
mcq.why: Both records were set at Swaraj Dweep, earlier called Havelock Island.

u0543.gist: The first conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels focused on cutting reliance on coal, oil and gas in a just, orderly, equitable way.
facts: Focus: reducing dependence on coal, oil and gas in a just, orderly and equitable manner.
Background: the COP28 Global Stocktake decision.
First principle: participation by those ready to move forward.
Second principle: implementation as the guiding star, based on shared scientific certainty.
Third principle: focus on solutions that support the transition rather than delay it.
u0543.hook: Three principles in three words: Ready, Implement, Solve.
u0543.trap: Its background is COP28's Global Stocktake, not COP30.

mcq.q: The First International Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels traces its background to which decision?
mcq.why: Its background lies in the COP28 Global Stocktake decision.

u0544.gist: India's first satellite-tagged Ganges soft-shell turtle, an endangered species, was released in Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve, Assam, on May 15, 2026.
facts: Released May 15, 2026 in the 1,302 sq. km Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve, Assam.
India's first satellite-tagged Ganges soft-shell turtle.
Species: Nilssonia gangetica; endangered; Schedule I under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
Identified by arrowhead-shaped markings on top of its head.
Five of India's soft-shell turtle species are known from the Kaziranga landscape.
u0544.hook: An arrow on its head points to the Ganges soft-shell turtle.

mcq.q: Where was India's first satellite-tagged Ganges soft-shell turtle released in May 2026?
mcq.why: It was released in Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve, Assam, on May 15, 2026.

u0545.gist: India ranks third worldwide in installed renewable capacity (250.50 GW at end-2025, per IRENA), behind China and the United States and ahead of Brazil.
facts: IRENA end-2025: China 2,258.02 GW, USA 466.45 GW, India 250.50 GW, Brazil 228.20 GW.
IRENA's July 2026 revision moved India from 250.52 GW to 250.50 GW; rank unchanged.
MNRE, 30 September 2026: renewables 299.247 GW + nuclear 8.780 GW = 308.027 GW non-fossil.
Solar (171.051 GW) and wind (59.201 GW) lead India's renewable capacity.
50% non-fossil capacity target met June 2025; share reached 54.18% on 30 June 2026.
FY 2025–26 generation: fossil 70.73%, non-fossil 29.27%.
u0545.hook: Top four order: China → USA → India → Brazil.
u0545.trap: Capacity share is not generation share: non-fossil was 54.18% of capacity (June 2026) but only 29.27% of FY 2025–26 generation.

mcq.q: According to IRENA's end-2025 comparison, which country ranks just behind India in installed renewable capacity?
mcq.why: India (250.50 GW) is third; Brazil follows with 228.20 GW.

mcq.q: As per MNRE, what was India's total non-fossil installed capacity on 30 September 2026?
mcq.why: Renewables 299.247 GW plus nuclear 8.780 GW gave 308.027 GW non-fossil.

u0546.gist: CMS COP15 in Campo Grande, Brazil (March 23–29, 2026), gave new or upgraded protection to 40 migratory species, subspecies and populations.
facts: CMS = Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals, also called the Bonn Convention.
COP15: Campo Grande, Brazil, March 23–29, 2026; theme 'Connecting Nature to Sustain Life'.
40 species, subspecies and populations added or upgraded in Appendices I and II.
CMS now covers over 1,200 unique species.
Brazil holds the CMS COP Presidency for the next three years.
COP16: Bonn, Germany, in 2029, marking CMS's 50th anniversary (signed at Bonn, 1979).
u0546.hook: Signed at Bonn in 1979 → back to Bonn in 2029 for its 50th birthday.
u0546.trap: CMS COP15 (Campo Grande) is a wildlife treaty meeting, not the UN climate COP.

mcq.q: Where was the 15th Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS COP15) held in March 2026?
mcq.why: CMS COP15 was held in Campo Grande, Brazil, from March 23 to 29, 2026.

mcq.q: How many species, subspecies and populations received new or upgraded protection at CMS COP15 in 2026?
mcq.why: COP15 gave new or upgraded protection to 40 species, subspecies and populations.

u0547.gist: Ladakh's Project Him Sarovar, launched on April 10, 2026 by LG Vinai Kumar Saxena, stores snowmelt and glacial melt in small reservoirs for lean periods.
facts: Launched April 10, 2026 by Vinai Kumar Saxena, Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh.
Water-security plan for Ladakh's cold desert: scientific snow harvesting, storing snowmelt and glacial melt.
Phase I: 50 water bodies (30 in Leh, 20 in Kargil), covering nearly 25% of villages.
By June 12, 2026, 5 reservoirs were complete; target 100 water bodies by next year.
u0547.hook: Him (snow) + Sarovar (lake) = lakes of stored snowmelt.
u0547.trap: 50 = Phase I water bodies; 100 = target for next year.

mcq.q: Under Phase I of Ladakh's Project Him Sarovar (2026), how many water bodies were proposed?
mcq.why: Phase I proposed 50 water bodies: 30 in Leh and 20 in Kargil.

u0548.gist: IQAir's 8th World Air Quality Report (March 24, 2026) covered 9,446 cities in 143 countries; only 14% of cities met WHO's PM2.5 guideline.
facts: Released March 24, 2026; 8th edition; covers 2025; 9,446 cities in 143 countries/regions.
Only 13 countries, regions and territories met WHO's annual PM2.5 guideline of 5 μg/m³.
Only 14% of global cities met the guideline in 2025, down from 17% in 2024.
Most polluted city: Loni, India (112.5 μg/m³); Delhi city fourth (99.6).
Most polluted country: Pakistan (67.3); India sixth (48.9).
Most polluted capital: New Delhi (82.2), then Dhaka (68.0) and Dushanbe (57.3).
u0548.hook: New Delhi tops the capitals at 82.2 while the WHO guideline is just 5.
u0548.trap: Loni, not Delhi, is the most polluted city (Delhi city is fourth); New Delhi tops only the capitals list. Also 13 = countries meeting the WHO guideline; 14% = share of cities.

mcq.q: Which was the most polluted capital city in IQAir's World Air Quality Report 2025, released in March 2026?
mcq.why: New Delhi topped the capitals with an average PM2.5 of 82.2 μg/m³.

mcq.q: Which city was the world's most polluted by annual average PM2.5 in 2025, per IQAir's World Air Quality Report?
mcq.why: Loni, India topped with 112.5 μg/m³, ahead of Hotan (109.6) and Byrnihat (101.1).

u0549.gist: On March 24, 2026, MoEFCC designated the 'Bhavasagara' Referral Centre at CMLRE, Kochi, as India's National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna.
facts: Designated on March 24, 2026 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Bhavasagara Referral Centre is at CMLRE (Centre for Marine Living Resources & Ecology), Kochi, Kerala.
CMLRE works under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).
Stores deep-sea animal collections from India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
Holds over 3560 identified, geo-referenced voucher specimens; supports deep-sea taxonomy training.
u0549.trap: Designated by MoEFCC, but CMLRE itself functions under MoES.

mcq.q: Which facility was designated India's National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna in March 2026?
mcq.why: MoEFCC designated the Bhavasagara Referral Centre at CMLRE, Kochi, on March 24, 2026.

u0550.gist: CSE's State of India's Environment 2026 (February 25, 2026) says 2025 saw the sharpest rise in extreme weather in four years, on 99% of days.
facts: Released by CSE and Down to Earth, February 25, 2026, at Anil Agarwal Dialogue, Nimli, near Alwar.
Jan 1–Nov 30, 2025: extreme weather on 99% of days; 4,419 deaths; 17.41 million hectares crops hit.
2024: 88% of days, 3,393 deaths; 2023: 89% of days, 3,208 deaths.
Worst-hit states: Himachal Pradesh (267 days), Kerala (173), Madhya Pradesh (162).
Only 15% of Indians (about 200 million) live within 10 km of a continuous air monitor.
Ocean acidity has risen 30–40% since the industrial era.
u0550.hook: Extreme-weather days: 89% (2023) → 88% (2024) → 99% (2025), almost every day of 2025.
u0550.trap: The SOE series began in 2014; CSE's Citizen's First Report dates to 1982.

mcq.q: According to CSE's State of India's Environment 2026 report, which state was worst hit by extreme weather in 2025?
mcq.why: Himachal Pradesh had extreme weather on 267 days, ahead of Kerala (173) and Madhya Pradesh (162).

mcq.q: Per the State of India's Environment 2026 report, on what share of days did India face extreme weather from January 1 to November 30, 2025?
mcq.why: Extreme weather occurred on 99% of days in that period of 2025.

u0551.gist: The Sixteenth IRENA Assembly ended on 12 January 2026 in Abu Dhabi, UAE, under the theme 'Powering Humanity: Renewable Energy for Shared Prosperity'.
facts: Sixteenth Session of the IRENA Assembly concluded on 12 January 2026.
Venue: Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
Theme: 'Powering Humanity: Renewable Energy for Shared Prosperity'.
IRENA Youth Forum on the sidelines: young leaders from more than 60 countries.

mcq.q: Where was the Sixteenth Session of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) Assembly held in January 2026?
mcq.why: The Sixteenth IRENA Assembly concluded on 12 January 2026 in Abu Dhabi, UAE.

u0552.gist: Rajnath Singh commissioned ICGS Samudra Pratap, India's first indigenously designed pollution control vessel, built by Goa Shipyard, in Goa on January 05, 2026.
facts: Commissioned by Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh in Goa on January 05, 2026.
First of two Pollution Control Vessels built by Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL).
India's first indigenously designed pollution control vessel; over 60% indigenous content.
Largest ship in the Indian Coast Guard fleet to date.
Built mainly for pollution control, but its role is wider.
u0552.trap: It is an Indian Coast Guard Ship (ICGS), not an Indian Navy ship (INS).

mcq.q: Which shipyard built ICGS Samudra Pratap, India's first indigenously designed pollution control vessel, commissioned in January 2026?
mcq.why: It is the first of two Pollution Control Vessels built by Goa Shipyard Limited.

u0553.gist: The Global Methane Status Report, launched on 17 November 2025 at COP30 in Belém, shows agriculture as the largest source of human-caused methane.
facts: Launched 17 November 2025 during COP30 in Belém, Brazil.
UNEP says the GMP includes 159 countries plus the European Commission.
As of April 2025, GMP members covered about 57% of global human-caused methane emissions.
Sector shares: agriculture about 42%, energy 38%, waste 20%.
G20+ countries: about 65% of emissions and 72% of technical mitigation potential by 2030.
u0553.trap: 57% = share covered by GMP members; 65% = share emitted by G20+ countries.
u0553.check: The text never expands 'GMP' and does not clearly name who published the report; 'technicale' is a typo.

mcq.q: According to the Global Methane Status Report (November 2025), which sector has the largest share of global anthropogenic methane?
mcq.why: Shares: agriculture about 42%, energy 38% and waste 20%.

u0554.gist: COP30 in Belém (November 10-22, 2025) shifted climate talks to implementation, producing the Belém Package of about 29 decisions built on the Global Mutirão decision.
facts: Held in Belém, Amazon region, November 10-22, 2025; an 'implementation-first' COP.
Belém Package: around 29 decisions as an implementation toolkit, based on the Global Mutirão decision.
Two-year Climate Finance Work Programme launched; Paris Agreement Article 9.1 reading strengthened.
Tropical Forest Forever Facility: Brazil-led, targets USD 125 billion; pays for protecting tropical forests.
Belém 4x Pledge: quadruple sustainable fuels by 2035 vs 2024; 23 countries endorsed; IEA tracks.
India: climate finance a legal obligation, demanded USD 1.3 trillion/year; opposed EU's CBAM.
u0554.hook: Mutirão (Brazil) ≈ Shramdaan (India): a community coming together for shared work.
u0554.trap: Belém Health Action Plan = first international climate adaptation plan only for health (USD 300 million); Belém Action Mechanism = just transition. Don't mix.

mcq.q: The 'Belém Package' adopted at COP30 (2025) was conceptually founded on which decision?
mcq.why: The package's conceptual foundation was the Global Mutirão decision.

mcq.q: Under COP30's Belém 4x Pledge, sustainable fuel use is to be quadrupled by which year, relative to 2024?
mcq.why: The pledge targets quadrupling sustainable fuels by 2035 relative to 2024; the IEA tracks it.
